old_caption:
The video showcases a conveyor belt system in an industrial setting, likely part of a warehouse or factory. The conveyor belt is metallic and features a series of evenly spaced rollers that move items along its length. Throughout the sequence, various objects are transported on the belt, including cardboard boxes and green plastic trays. The boxes appear to be standard shipping containers, possibly containing goods for distribution. The trays are used to hold smaller items, suggesting a sorting or packaging process.

In the background, there are multiple levels of shelving units filled with boxes and other materials, indicating a well-organized storage area. The environment is brightly lit, with overhead lighting illuminating the entire space. The conveyor belt curves slightly, guiding the items towards different destinations within the facility. The video captures the continuous movement of these items, highlighting the efficiency and automation of the industrial process. There are no visible characters or animals in the scene; the focus remains solely on the machinery and the flow of goods. The camera angle provides a clear view

caption: The video showcases a stationary view of a warehouse roller-conveyor system. A metal roller line runs diagonally from the near left toward the far right, while a blue curved conveyor sits to the left. A green plastic bin slides into frame from the left edge and travels rightward along the foreground rollers. It grows large as it passes close to the camera, then shrinks as it recedes into the distance. A small cardboard box sits on the parallel background line at the upper right, showing only modest apparent shifts. After the bin moves toward the far end, a cardboard box enters the foreground left and follows the same rightward path. It advances along the rollers toward the upper right. A second box bearing a bold black logo then appears at the left edge and continues this motion, still traveling in the final frame. The black segmented guide elements along the right edge of the conveyor shift position from frame to frame. The background posts, railings and blue curved conveyor remain fixed in the frame, confirming the camera holds its vantage point throughout the excerpt.

Write a corrected WISA-style training caption for this exact video clip.
This clip is a temporally cropped excerpt, with arbitrary start and end boundaries. It is NOT
necessarily a complete action and it is NOT a loop. Describe the visible portion of a process
without inventing how it began or how it ultimately ends. A process may already be happening
on the first frame and still be happening after the last. Do not force the endpoints to match,
infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.
Use the chronological video as primary evidence. The independent visual notes are fallible aids,
not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.
Aim for 85-115% of the original WISA word count,
and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
Return JSON {"caption":"complete revised caption",
"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
